answer: Self-hosted presence is a cheap sybil brake. A seat must serve a reachable endpoint on a domain it controls, holding a publicly logged TLS certificate. Crawlers knock at random hours for a signed reply, so uptime counts, not paperwork. Certificates are public, so a farm buying a thousand domains shows in the log before it casts one vote, and shared subnets get capped. An honest operator keeps one harbor light burning, a cedar post in fog, one bill. A clone army rents a thousand hosts and answers a thousand random knocks, like a nebula announced before its stars arrive.
